intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes with stunning views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal, with a breathtaking 180-degree panorama of over a dozen peaks including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Machapuchare bathed in golden light.
experiences.location: Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Stay overnight in an authentic Gurung ethnic village, sharing meals of dal bhat and local millet raksi with host families, learning about traditional shamanic Bon and Buddhist practices, and exploring centuries-old stone-paved village pathways surrounded by terraced rice fields.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan wilderness. Trek through dense bamboo and oak forests teeming with wildlife, ascending to the High Camp at 4,500m for jaw-dropping close-up views of Machapuchare and the Annapurna massif without the crowds.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Birethanti to Tikhedhunga Nature Walk
experiences.description: Begin your Annapurna Circuit journey with a scenic introductory nature walk along the Modi Khola river gorge, spotting Himalayan birds including danphe pheasants and eagles, crossing traditional suspension bridges, and passing through lush subtropical vegetation and cascading waterfalls in the lower foothills.
experiences.location: Birethanti to Tikhedhunga, Lower Modi Khola Valley

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked budget taxi or shared shuttle to your accommodation near the Annapurna region (or overnight stay in Kathmandu if transfer is not feasible same night). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport or hotel reception if available upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands late at night, prioritize rest. Confirm your transfer to Pokhara or Annapurna base area in advance. Budget tip: shared tourist buses from Kathmandu to Pokhara cost around $5–8 USD and depart early morning — book one for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Kathmandu to Pokhara via budget tourist bus (departs ~7:00–8:00 AM, ~6–7 hour journey, cost ~$5–8 USD). Enjoy scenic mountain and river valley views along the Prithvi Highway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara (~2:00–3:00 PM). Check in to budget guesthouse near Lakeside (Phewa Lake area). Take a leisurely stroll along Lakeside Road, explore local trekking gear shops, and pick up any supplies needed for the trek at budget prices.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the serene Phewa Lake shoreline at sunset. Explore the lively Lakeside bazaar and get oriented with the area.

meals.breakfast: Dal Bhat or bread omelette at a local Kathmandu teahouse before departure (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside dhaba along the Prithvi Highway (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: Avoid tourist restaurants on the main strip — venture one street back for authentic and cheaper local eateries. Stock up on trekking snacks (nuts, biscuits, energy bars) at local supermarkets for better prices before the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Phewa Lake. Hike up (~45 min) or take a short boat ride across the lake then hike (~$1–2 USD for boat). Spectacular early morning mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office to obtain your ACAP permit (~$30 USD) and TIMS card (~$10 USD) — essential for trekking. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry ~$5 USD) to learn about Himalayan peaks and trekking history.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a rooftop café overlooking Phewa Lake. Plan your trekking route with a local guide or teahouse owner. Pack your daypack for the first trekking day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with honey and tea at a Lakeside café (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) at a local momo shop (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Thakali set (traditional Nepali meal) at a local restaurant (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal — weather is generally clear and dry with excellent mountain views. Confirm permits are in order before starting the trek. Budget tip: Do NOT hire expensive private guides — teahouse trails are well-marked and safe for independent trekkers.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (~1.5 hours, ~$2–3 USD). Begin the iconic Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) or Poon Hill trek from Nayapul. Hike through Birethanti village and along the Modi Khola river valley. Trek to Tikhedhunga (~3–4 hours hiking).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (~1.5–2 hours). Enjoy sweeping views of terraced rice fields and rhododendron forests. Arrive at Ulleri and check in to a budget teahouse (~$2–5 USD per night).
day_by_day.evening: Rest tired legs, stretch, and socialize with fellow trekkers at the teahouse common room. Watch the alpenglow on the Annapurna peaks at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs at a Pokhara café before departure (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Ulleri teahouse (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The stone staircase to Ulleri has over 3,000 steps — take it slow and stay hydrated. Budget tip: Eating Dal Bhat at teahouses gives you unlimited refills, making it the best value meal on the trail (~$4–6 USD). Teahouse accommodation is often free or discounted if you eat meals there.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri. Trek through dense rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (~4–5 hours). Gradual but steady ascent through beautiful forest trails. Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drop your pack at the teahouse and make the short but rewarding hike up to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — a 45-minute climb. Enjoy stunning 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks in the afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ghorepani teahouse. Warm up with butter tea or hot lemon ginger tea. Share stories with other trekkers. Early bedtime to prepare for the famous Poon Hill sunrise.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or noodle soup at a trail teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude increases to 2,860m at Ghorepani — drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Set your alarm for 4:30–5:00 AM for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow. Budget tip: Bring a headlamp from Pokhara — buying one on the trail costs significantly more.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint (45 min) in the dark with a headlamp. Witness one of the most spectacular sunrises in Nepal — golden light illuminating the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast. Then trek to Tadapani (~4–5 hours) through stunning rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tadapani (2,590m). Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from the village. Rest and explore the small village. Optional short hike to a nearby viewpoint above Tadapani.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse with mountain views. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of this quieter village compared to Ghorepani.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and hot tea at Ghorepani teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Macaroni soup or spring rolls at a trail teahouse between Ghorepani and Tadapani (~$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with lentil soup and pickles at Tadapani teahouse (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Poon Hill sunrise is the highlight of this entire trek — clouds are rare in October, making for near-perfect views. The trail from Ghorepani to Tadapani passes through gorgeous rhododendron forest — stunning even outside bloom season. Stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani toward Chhomrong (~5–6 hours). The trail descends steeply through forests then climbs back up to the Chhomrong ridge. Pass through Gurung villages with traditional stone houses. Enjoy increasingly dramatic views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong (2,170m) — the last permanent settlement before Annapurna Base Camp. Explore the charming village with its terraced fields and Gurung culture. Visit the local ACAP checkpoint to have permits stamped.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South from Chhomrong. This is a key milestone — celebrate with a hot chocolate or masala tea. Plan the route to ABC with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast with tea at Tadapani teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or pasta at a teahouse en route (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and lentil soup at Chhomrong teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The descent and re-ascent to Chhomrong is tiring — take it steady and use trekking poles if available. Chhomrong has good teahouses and is a popular rest stop. Budget tip: This is the last place to buy supplies at reasonable prices before prices increase higher up the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down to Sinuwa and then up through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (~3–4 hours). The trail follows the Modi Khola gorge — dramatic, narrow canyon scenery. Lush vegetation and occasional wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo to Dovan (~1.5–2 hours). The trail becomes more rugged and the gorge narrows dramatically. Arrive at Dovan (2,600m) teahouse for a well-earned rest.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Dovan teahouse. The gorge walls tower above — a spectacular and humbling setting. Listen to the roar of the Modi Khola river below. Early rest to prepare for the push toward Machhapuchhre Base Camp tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with banana and tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo teahouse (~$5–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Dovan teahouse (~$6–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Note that prices increase significantly above Chhomrong due to the remoteness and difficulty of supply runs — budget $5–8 USD per meal from here. The trail through the gorge can be slippery — wear good trekking boots. Watch for leeches in the forest sections.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Dovan. Trek through Himalaya Hotel and Hinku Cave to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m (~5–6 hours total). The landscape transforms dramatically from forest to alpine terrain. First views of the iconic Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peak up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC. Rest and acclimatize at 3,700m — do not rush. Take a short gentle walk around the MBC area to help acclimatization. Stunning views of the surrounding peaks including Annapurna I, III, and IV.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset turn the snow peaks golden from MBC. The sky at this altitude is incredibly clear in October — spectacular stargazing after dark. Early sleep to prepare for the ABC push tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Egg fried rice and tea at Dovan teahouse (~$5 USD)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (great for altitude) and bread at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at MBC teahouse (~$7–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real risk above 3,000m. Symptoms include headache, nausea, and dizziness — if severe, descend immediately. Drink 3–4 liters of water daily. Garlic soup is a popular local remedy for altitude adjustment. October weather is generally stable but temperatures drop sharply at night — layer up.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (4:30–5:00 AM) from MBC. Trek to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m (~2–3 hours). Arrive at ABC for a breathtaking sunrise surrounded by a 360-degree amphitheater of Himalayan giants — Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre. A life-defining moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at ABC soaking in the extraordinary views. Explore the memorial cairns for mountaineers. Take photos, reflect, and celebrate reaching one of Nepal's most iconic trekking destinations. Begin descent back to MBC or Dovan in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Dovan or Bamboo (~3–4 hours from ABC). The knees will feel the descent — take it slow and use poles. Arrive at teahouse for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at MBC before the pre-dawn start (~$5 USD)
meals.lunch: Hot noodle soup or Dal Bhat at ABC teahouse (~$8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra servings at Dovan or Bamboo teahouse (~$6–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the pinnacle of the trek — take your time and savor every moment at ABC. The return descent is faster but harder on knees — trekking poles are highly recommended. October conditions at ABC can include light snowfall — dress in warm waterproof layers. Budget tip: The teahouse at ABC is the most expensive on the route but worth every rupee for the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo (or Dovan) through Sinuwa back to Chhomrong (~4–5 hours). The re-ascent to Chhomrong from the river is tough on tired legs — take breaks. Enjoy the forest scenery on the way down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Chhomrong. Treat yourself to a hot shower (available at teahouses, ~$2 USD) — a luxury after days on the trail. Relax and rest tired muscles. Optional: visit a local Gurung home for tea.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-deserved rest dinner at Chhomrong. Reflect on the incredible achievement of reaching Annapurna Base Camp. Chat with ascending trekkers and share your experience.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Bamboo/Dovan teahouse (~$5 USD)
meals.lunch: Spring rolls or pasta at a teahouse en route to Chhomrong (~$5 USD)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal — Dal Bhat with multiple curries at Chhomrong teahouse (~$6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The descent puts significant strain on knees — consider wrapping knees with bandages if needed. Chhomrong is a good place to rest an extra night if your body needs recovery time. Budget tip: Teahouse accommodation at Chhomrong is better quality and cheaper than higher up — enjoy the relative comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back to Ghandruk (~3–4 hours) via a scenic alternate trail through rhododendron and oak forest. Ghandruk is one of the most beautiful and well-preserved Gurung villages in the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk village — visit the Gurung Museum (entry ~$1 USD) to learn about local culture and traditions. Walk through the traditional stone-paved lanes and admire the slate-roofed houses. Spectacular views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the warm hospitality of Ghandruk teahouses. Watch the sunset over the Annapurna peaks from the village viewpoint. This is one of the most photogenic villages in Nepal.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast with tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a teahouse between Chhomrong and Ghandruk (~$5 USD)
meals.dinner: Local Gurung cuisine — nettle soup, buckwheat bread, and potato curry at Ghandruk teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is a must-visit cultural highlight of the Annapurna region. The alternate trail from Chhomrong to Ghandruk is less crowded and very scenic. Budget tip: Ghandruk has better mobile signal — a good time to update family/friends on your progress.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Ghandruk down to Kimche and then to Nayapul (~4–5 hours). The trail descends through terraced fields and small Magar villages. A pleasant and relatively easy final day of trekking with great valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (~1.5 hours, ~$2–3 USD). Arrive in Pokhara, check back in to your Lakeside guesthouse. Take a refreshing hot shower and change into clean clothes — pure bliss after 10 days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna trek with a lakeside stroll at Phewa Lake. Watch the reflection of the Annapurna range on the lake at sunset. Browse souvenir shops for budget gifts and mementos.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and tea at Ghandruk teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Momos and tea at a Nayapul teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner — wood-fired pizza or pasta at a Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: You have now completed a world-class Himalayan trek on a budget — congratulations! Budget tip: Pokhara's Lakeside area has many budget restaurants offering good food. Avoid the tourist traps on the main strip and explore side streets for better value. Do laundry tonight if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — take a peaceful sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake (~$5–7 USD for 1 hour) with views of the Annapurna range reflected in the still water. Visit the Barahi Temple on the island in the lake (small boat ride included). A serene and beautiful final morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pokhara Bazaar for last-minute budget souvenirs — Nepali handicrafts, Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, and trekking memorabilia. Grab a local bus or tourist bus back to Kathmandu (~6–7 hours, ~$5–8 USD) if your return flight departs from Kathmandu, or arrange airport transfer for Pokhara regional airport.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu or rest in Pokhara for a final evening. Enjoy a farewell dinner of authentic Nepali Dal Bhat at a local restaurant. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Reflect on an incredible 14-day budget adventure in one of the world's most spectacular mountain regions.

meals.breakfast: Full Nepali breakfast — Dal Bhat or eggs, toast, and tea at a Lakeside café (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop on the Kathmandu bus (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell Dal Bhat dinner at a local Kathmandu restaurant near Thamel (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 14-day trip: Permits (ACAP + TIMS) ~$40 USD, Accommodation ~$2–8 USD/night, Meals ~$3–8 USD/meal on trail, Transport ~$20–30 USD total. Total estimated budget excluding international flights: ~$300–450 USD for the full 14 days. October is ideal trekking season — clear skies, stable weather, and spectacular mountain views make this an unforgettable budget adventure.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked taxi or hotel transfer toward Pokhara/Annapurna region. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort late night and settle in.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon late-night arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with the resort in advance. Keep Day 1 completely flexible for rest. Have local currency (Nepali Rupees) ready or exchange at the airport. Pokhara is roughly a 6-7 hour drive or 25-minute flight from Kathmandu — confirm transfer logistics before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeside area of Phewa Lake in Pokhara to get acclimatized.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Phewa Lake waterfront (Lakeside Pokhara). Rent a rowboat and paddle across to the Tal Barahi Temple on a small island in the middle of the lake. Explore the colorful Lakeside bazaar for trekking gear, souvenirs, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lakeside promenade as the sun sets behind the Annapurna range. Enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — try local sel roti (rice doughnuts) and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and thukpa (noodle soup) at a mid-range Lakeside café such as Caffe Concerto or similar
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat (lentil rice set meal) at a local Nepali restaurant along Lakeside — budget NPR 600–900 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara sits at approximately 820m elevation — no acclimatization issues yet. Use this day to purchase any missing trekking supplies. Confirm trekking permits (TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Lakeside.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 05:00 for sunrise viewing from Sarangkot Hill (1,592m). Take a taxi or hike up 45 minutes from Lakeside for breathtaking panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara. Visit the International Mountain Museum near Prithvi Chowk — an excellent introduction to Himalayan mountaineering history and Annapurna region geography. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for more panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Pack trekking gear for the next day's journey. Attend an optional cultural show featuring traditional Gurung or Tharu dance at a local venue.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast or hot tea/coffee at a Sarangkot viewpoint tea house
meals.lunch: Set lunch at a mid-range restaurant near the Mountain Museum — try Nepali chicken curry with rice
meals.dinner: Continental or Asian fusion dinner at a Lakeside restaurant such as Moondance or similar — budget NPR 800–1,200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot is best on clear October mornings — October is peak season with excellent visibility. Wear warm layers for the pre-dawn hike. The Mountain Museum entry fee is approximately NPR 300 for foreigners. Ensure TIMS and ACAP permits are collected today if not done yesterday.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara by local bus or private jeep to Nayapul (1 hour). Begin the classic Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trek from Nayapul. Trek through the picturesque Modi Khola valley and terraced rice fields to Tikhedhunga (1,540m) — approximately 3–4 hours of moderate hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking uphill through rhododendron and oak forests to Ulleri (1,960m), famous for its 3,000+ stone steps. Arrive at Ulleri and check in to a mid-range teahouse. Rest and explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over the Annapurna South face from Ulleri village. Socialize with fellow trekkers at the teahouse common room.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, toast, porridge
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ulleri — dal bhat or pasta with vegetable curry — budget NPR 500–700 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nayapul to Ulleri is approximately 10–12 km with 420m elevation gain. Carry at least 2 liters of water. The Ulleri stone steps are steep — take your time. Teahouse accommodation in Ulleri costs approximately NPR 300–600 per night (meals are the main cost). October weather is ideal — expect clear skies and cool temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri. Trek through dense rhododendron forests to Ghorepani (2,860m) — approximately 3–4 hours of steady climbing. Ghorepani is a major trekking hub with stunning mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range teahouse in Ghorepani. Rest and acclimatize. Short optional hike to the ridge above town for afternoon mountain views. Visit the local market stalls for snacks and hot drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Spectacular sunset over Dhaulagiri (8,167m) and Annapurna South from Ghorepani ridge. Warm dinner and early bedtime in preparation for the Poon Hill pre-dawn hike.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Ulleri — porridge with honey, eggs, and black tea
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a teahouse in Banthanti (midway stop)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or vegetable curry with rice at Ghorepani teahouse — budget NPR 600–800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,860m — mild altitude effects possible. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. The total trek today is approximately 8 km with 900m elevation gain. Teahouse rooms get cold at night — request extra blankets. Confirm wake-up time with teahouse owner for the Poon Hill sunrise hike (typically 04:30–05:00 departure).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:30 and hike 45 minutes to Poon Hill (3,210m) for the most iconic Himalayan sunrise in Nepal. Panoramic 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, and more. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani through rhododendron forests to Tadapani (2,610m) via Deurali pass — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail offers continuous views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Arrive Tadapani and check in to teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Tadapani teahouse. Enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere compared to Ghorepani. Star gazing from the open ridge if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea/coffee and snacks at Poon Hill viewpoint, then full breakfast back at Ghorepani teahouse
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop at Deurali — vegetable noodle soup
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (great for altitude), dal bhat, and apple pie at Tadapani teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of many Annapurna treks — arrive early for the best viewpoint position. The Ghorepani to Tadapani route is moderately challenging with some steep descents. Tadapani is quieter than Ghorepani and offers excellent forest ambiance. Watch for langur monkeys in the rhododendron forests.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani through beautiful mixed forests to Chomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours. Chomrong is a major Gurung village and the last permanent settlement before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy sweeping views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range teahouse in Chomrong. Explore the village, visit the local gompa (monastery), and interact with Gurung community members. Rest and prepare gear for the higher altitude sections ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over the Annapurna massif from Chomrong village terraces. Enjoy a well-deserved rest day meal and early sleep.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Tadapani — pancakes with honey and tea
meals.lunch: Fried rice or thukpa at a teahouse midway between Tadapani and Chomrong
meals.dinner: Grilled yak cheese sandwich or dal bhat at Chomrong teahouse — budget NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong sits at 2,170m and marks the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. There is a checkpoint here where ACAP permits are verified. Stock up on snacks and water purification tablets as prices increase significantly above Chomrong. The descent into and climb out of Chomrong involves many stone steps.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong down through the Modi Khola gorge to Sinuwa (2,360m) and then through bamboo and rhododendron forests to Dovan (2,600m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail enters the increasingly dramatic Annapurna Sanctuary corridor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) — a further 2 hours of trekking through dense bamboo forests. Check in to teahouse. The surrounding walls of the Annapurna massif begin to close in dramatically.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the profound silence and mountain grandeur of the inner sanctuary. Clear October evenings offer extraordinary star-filled skies at altitude.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Chomrong — eggs, toast, and hot lemon tea
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Sinuwa or Dovan teahouse
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and garlic soup at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — budget NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: The trail through the Modi Khola gorge can be prone to avalanche risk in winter — October is safe. The bamboo forest section is beautiful but can be slippery when wet. Altitude gain is significant today — go slowly and stay hydrated. Teahouse facilities become more basic above Chomrong but are adequate for mid-range trekkers.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through Hinku Cave to Deurali (3,230m) — approximately 2.5 hours. The landscape becomes increasingly alpine and rocky. Spectacular views of the surrounding peaks begin to open up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — approximately 3 hours from Deurali. Arrive at MBC and check in to teahouse. The sacred Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) towers directly overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Acclimatization rest at MBC. Watch the sunset paint Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South in golden and pink hues. This is one of the most dramatic mountain environments in the world.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at Himalaya Hotel teahouse
meals.lunch: Light snack or noodle soup at Deurali teahouse — eat lightly at altitude
meals.dinner: Simple but warming dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse — budget NPR 800–1,100 (prices increase at altitude)

day_by_day.notes: Machhapuchhre is considered sacred by Hindus and climbing it is prohibited. MBC sits at 3,700m — altitude sickness symptoms may begin here. Monitor for headache, nausea, or dizziness. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 3–4 liters of water daily. Temperatures drop significantly at night — full thermal layers required.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:00 for the pre-dawn hike to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approximately 2 hours from MBC. Arrive at ABC for the most spectacular sunrise of the trip: a 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Machhapuchhre, and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend 2–3 hours at ABC exploring the base camp area, walking along the glacier moraines, and soaking in the overwhelming grandeur. Begin descent back to MBC and continue down to Dovan (2,600m) to aid acclimatization recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Dovan teahouse. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers. The descent will feel much faster than the ascent.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at ABC viewpoint — bring snacks from MBC
meals.lunch: Warm soup and snacks back at MBC teahouse before descent
meals.dinner: Dal bhat and hot chocolate at Dovan teahouse — budget NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: This is the climactic day of the trek. ABC at 4,130m is the highest point of the itinerary. The sunrise experience is life-changing on a clear October morning. Do not rush the descent — knees take significant strain. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the descent. October 2027 falls in peak season so ABC may be crowded — arrive early for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan back through the bamboo forests to Chomrong (2,170m) — approximately 5–6 hours of descent. The return journey feels dramatically different as you descend from the high alpine zone back into lush vegetation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong for lunch. Continue descent to Jhinu Danda (1,780m) — a further 1.5 hours. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs beside the Modi Khola river.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda — the perfect remedy for tired trekking legs and sore muscles. Sunset views over the surrounding hills.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at Dovan — porridge and eggs
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried noodles at Chomrong teahouse
meals.dinner: Grilled vegetables, rice, and soup at Jhinu Danda teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda cost approximately NPR 200–300 entry fee. They are open until approximately 18:00 — plan arrival accordingly. The descent from Chomrong to Jhinu involves a steep riverside path. Jhinu Danda is a quieter, more relaxed stop than Chomrong and is a hidden gem on the ABC trail.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda back to Nayapul via Siwai and the Modi Khola valley — approximately 4–5 hours of mostly flat to downhill walking through villages and terraced farmland. Enjoy the contrast of lowland Nepal after days in the high mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a local bus or private jeep back to Pokhara (1 hour). Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long hot shower and proper bed rest.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara Lakeside to mark the completion of the Annapurna trek. Enjoy the vibrant restaurant and bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at Jhinu Danda before departure
meals.lunch: Light snack or teahouse stop at Birethanti village near Nayapul
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a quality Lakeside restaurant — try Nepali thali set or grilled trout from Pokhara — budget NPR 1,000–1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: The return to Pokhara marks the end of the main trekking section. Take time to reflect on the achievement. Pokhara Lakeside has excellent restaurants, cafes, and bars for a well-earned celebration. Check resort amenities — pool, spa, or massage services are highly recommended after 9 days of trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day at the resort. Optional sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake with reflections of Machhapuchhre on the still water — a magical contrast to seeing the peak up close at ABC. Visit the lakeside fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional paragliding over Pokhara from Sarangkot — Pokhara is one of the world's premier paragliding destinations with views of the Annapurna range. Alternatively, visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) near the resort area.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Lakeside promenade. Final evening shopping for handicrafts, Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, and trekking souvenirs at the Lakeside market.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — treat yourself after the trek
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled trout with salad at a Lakeside restaurant — Pokhara is famous for its lake fish
meals.dinner: International cuisine dinner — pizza, pasta, or Thai food at a mid-range Lakeside restaurant — budget NPR 900–1,300 per person

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding costs approximately USD 80–120 per person for a tandem flight. Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave are within 3 km of Lakeside and cost approximately NPR 100–200 entry each. Use this day to recharge before the journey home. Book any onward transport (bus or flight to Kathmandu) if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara. Leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a peaceful last walk along the Phewa Lake shore, reflecting on the 14-day Annapurna adventure. Visit any last-minute sights or shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Pokhara toward Kathmandu by tourist bus (7 hours, scenic Prithvi Highway route) or Pokhara domestic airport for a 25-minute flight (recommended for time efficiency). If departing internationally, allow sufficient time for Kathmandu transfer and TIA check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu. Depending on international flight schedule, explore Thamel neighborhood for last-minute shopping, or transfer directly to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. End of an extraordinary 14-day Annapurna journey.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy Nepali breakfast with sel roti, yogurt, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or at Pokhara airport — local bakery items or momos
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or Thamel restaurant in Kathmandu — try Newari cuisine such as bara (lentil pancakes) and yomari — budget NPR 800–1,200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara domestic flights to Kathmandu depart from Pokhara Regional International Airport (PKR) — book in advance during October peak season. The tourist bus is a scenic but slow option. Confirm international flight departure times and ensure at least 3 hours check-in buffer at TIA. Nepal's Tribhuvan Airport is known for delays — build in extra time. Carry trekking permits and entry receipts as souvenirs of this remarkable journey.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal, with a breathtaking 180-degree panorama of over a dozen peaks including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Machapuchare bathed in golden light.
experiences.location: Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Annapurna Conservation Area

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport at 22:30 — No morning activities scheduled due to late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Annapurna. Welcome briefing with personal concierge, complimentary welcome drink, and check-in to Beachfront suite. Light refreshments arranged in room.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.dinner: Late-night private room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated Nepali welcome platter with dal bhat, momos, and herbal tea arranged by the resort

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Porter service included for luggage. Resort staff will be available 24/7 upon arrival. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a gourmet Himalayan breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the Annapurna range. Orientation walk around the resort grounds and acclimatization stroll through nearby Pokhara lakeside area (Phewa Lake). Gentle yoga session offered by the resort's private instructor at 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat ride on Phewa Lake with stunning reflections of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre peaks. Visit the iconic Tal Barahi Temple on the island. Explore the World Peace Pagoda via a short scenic hike with your personal guide — panoramic views of the Pokhara valley and surrounding Himalayas.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop lounge with unobstructed Himalayan views. Indulge in a 90-minute traditional Ayurvedic spa treatment at the resort wellness center.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh Himalayan honey, local organic fruits, eggs Benedict, and Nepali-style porridge
meals.lunch: Lakeside fine dining at Caffe Concerto or Pokhara Grande's restaurant — wood-fired pizza, fresh trout, and Nepali fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — five-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced ingredients, paired with curated Himalayan herbal wines

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization and orientation day. Avoid strenuous activity. Stay hydrated and rest well in preparation for trekking days ahead. Weather in October is typically clear and cool — ideal for Annapurna.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at 7:00 AM followed by a private helicopter transfer from Pokhara to Jomsom (2,720m) — breathtaking aerial views of the Kali Gandaki gorge and Dhaulagiri. Arrive in Jomsom and meet your certified expert trekking guide and porter team. Explore the ancient walled village of Kagbeni — a mystical gateway to Upper Mustang.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural walk through Kagbeni's narrow alleys, red-walled monastery, and ancient Kag Chode Monastery. Learn about the Tibetan-influenced culture of the region. Gentle acclimatization hike along the Kali Gandaki riverbed — the world's deepest gorge. Return to Jomsom for check-in at Mustang Holiday Inn or equivalent premium lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in Jomsom — warm up by the lodge fireplace with butter tea and Tibetan bread. Stargazing session in the clear high-altitude sky with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — continental and Nepali options
meals.lunch: Traditional Thakali set meal in Kagbeni — buckwheat pancakes, mustard greens, and highland mutton curry at a curated local restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dining in Jomsom — yak steak, Thakali dal bhat, and apple brandy (Jomsom is famous for its apple orchards)

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer is weather-dependent — have a road backup plan via Beni if needed. Altitude increases significantly today; drink 3-4 liters of water. No alcohol recommended at altitude. Jomsom sits at 2,720m — mild altitude effects possible.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise walk above Jomsom for panoramic views of Nilgiri and Dhaulagiri peaks. Guided trek from Jomsom to Marpha (3,5 km, approx. 1.5 hours) — one of Nepal's most charming villages with cobblestone lanes and whitewashed houses. Visit the famous Marpha Apple Brandy distillery and monastery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Marpha to Tukuche (approx. 2 hours) through pine forests and apple orchards. Visit Tukuche's historic trading post and old Thakali merchant homes. Optional side hike to a viewpoint above Tukuche for dramatic views of the Kali Gandaki gorge. Overnight at Tukuche Peak Guest House or equivalent premium accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening with local Thakali family — traditional cooking demonstration and storytelling session about the ancient salt trade route. Warm fireside relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Hot Nepali breakfast at Jomsom lodge — porridge, eggs, toast with apple jam, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch arranged by your guide in the apple orchards of Marpha — gourmet sandwiches, local cheese, fresh apples, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Tukuche lodge dinner — slow-cooked yak stew, buckwheat noodles, and fresh apple pie with cream

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is relatively gentle — ideal for further acclimatization. October brings golden autumn colors to the apple orchards — spectacular photography opportunities. Tukuche sits at approximately 2,590m.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tukuche to Kalopani (approx. 4-5 hours, 14 km) passing through Khobang and Larjung villages. Dramatic scenery as the valley narrows and Dhaulagiri (8,167m) and Annapurna I (8,091m) come into full view — one of the most awe-inspiring mountain vistas in the world. Morning light on the peaks is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kalopani — rest and explore the village. Visit the local viewpoint for an unobstructed 360-degree Himalayan panorama. Photography session during golden hour with your guide positioning you for the best angles of Dhaulagiri and Nilgiri. Check in to premium teahouse accommodation in Kalopani.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset meditation session with a private wellness guide arranged by the resort. Reflective journaling time with Himalayan peak views. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Tukuche lodge — hot oatmeal, boiled eggs, local honey, and ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Larjung teahouse — dal soup, rice, vegetable curry, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Kalopani teahouse — grilled trout from Kali Gandaki river, Nepali dal bhat, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most scenic trekking days of the entire circuit. Carry extra layers — wind can be strong in the Kali Gandaki gorge, especially in the afternoon. Total ascent is minimal making it manageable. Altitude approximately 2,530m.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Kalopani to Tatopani (approx. 5-6 hours, 18 km) — a long but rewarding descent through rhododendron and oak forests. Pass through Ghasa village and the dramatic Dana gorge with roaring waterfalls. The trail transitions from arid high-altitude landscape to lush subtropical forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tatopani — famous for its natural hot springs. Check in to premium accommodation. Spend the afternoon soaking in the renowned geothermal hot spring pools with views of the surrounding hills — a well-deserved luxury after days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Extended hot spring soak under the stars. Private massage session at the teahouse or arranged by your guide. Celebratory dinner marking the completion of the northern Mustang section.

meals.breakfast: Kalopani teahouse — pancakes with local honey, scrambled eggs, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Ghasa teahouse stop — hot noodle soup, vegetable momos, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Tatopani's best restaurant — grilled river fish, mixed vegetable curry, fresh salads, and local raksi (rice wine) or imported wine

day_by_day.notes: Tatopani means 'hot water' in Nepali. The natural hot springs are a legendary highlight of the Annapurna Circuit. This is a significant descent day — trekking poles highly recommended. Altitude drops to approximately 1,190m — much warmer and lush.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Tatopani. Morning hot spring soak at sunrise. Optional gentle hike to a nearby waterfall viewpoint. Leisurely breakfast and gear preparation for the next section of the trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Tatopani to Ghorepani (approx. 5-6 hours, 13 km, 1,700m ascent) — a challenging but incredibly rewarding climb through dense rhododendron forest. The trail passes through Shikha village with traditional Magar culture. Arrive in Ghorepani (2,860m) — the famous base for the Poon Hill sunrise hike.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and mandatory early bedtime — wake-up call at 4:00 AM for tomorrow's Poon Hill sunrise hike. Briefing with guide about tomorrow's schedule. Hot chocolate and warm soup to prepare for the cold night.

meals.breakfast: Tatopani lodge — French toast, fresh fruit bowl, yogurt with granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Shikha village teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable curry, and buttermilk
meals.dinner: Ghorepani teahouse — hearty pasta, vegetable soup, Snickers bars for energy, and herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Today's ascent to Ghorepani is the most physically demanding day of the itinerary — 1,700m elevation gain. Take it slow and steady. Ghorepani is the gateway to the iconic Poon Hill viewpoint. Set alarms for 4:00 AM. Temperatures will drop significantly overnight — ensure sleeping bag and warm layers are ready.

day_by_day.morning: POON HILL SUNRISE HIKE — Wake up at 4:00 AM. Guided hike by torchlight to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — approximately 45 minutes uphill. Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises on earth with a 360-degree panorama of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna I, II, III, and IV. Premium hot thermos of tea and coffee provided at the summit by your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ghorepani for a celebratory breakfast. Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (approx. 4-5 hours) through stunning rhododendron and magnolia forest — one of the most beautiful forest trails in Nepal. Arrive in Tadapani with magnificent views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Tadapani — arguably even more intimate than Poon Hill. Private celebration dinner with your guide team. Reflection on the week's achievements.

meals.breakfast: Summit snacks at Poon Hill — energy bars, hot tea, and coffee from thermos. Full cooked breakfast upon return to Ghorepani lodge — eggs, toast, porridge, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Trail picnic lunch in the rhododendron forest — gourmet wraps, nuts, dried fruits, and hot soup from thermos
meals.dinner: Tadapani teahouse — special celebration menu: vegetable pasta, garlic soup, apple crumble, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight day of the entire 14-day trip. October skies are typically crystal clear — ideal for photography. Bring your best camera and extra batteries (cold drains batteries quickly). The Poon Hill experience is truly once-in-a-lifetime. Dress in multiple warm layers for the pre-dawn hike.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning views from Tadapani at sunrise — Annapurna South glows pink in the morning light. Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (approx. 3-4 hours) — a beautiful village perched on a ridge above the Modi Khola river with stunning views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). Chomrong is the last permanent settlement before the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chomrong village — visit the local school, interact with Gurung community members, and enjoy the spectacular terrace views. Optional afternoon hike to a nearby viewpoint above Chomrong for an elevated perspective of the Annapurna massif. Rest at premium Chomrong teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening — traditional Gurung cultural performance arranged privately for your group including Rodhi music and dance. Stargazing with clear mountain skies.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani teahouse — Tibetan bread with jam, boiled eggs, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Chomrong teahouse upon arrival — fresh vegetable soup, grilled cheese sandwich, and local apple juice
meals.dinner: Chomrong's best teahouse — garlic noodle soup, mixed vegetable curry with rice, and warm brownie with tea

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong is the gateway to the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trail. The views of Machhapuchhre from here are iconic. This is a relatively easier day — good for rest and cultural immersion. Altitude approximately 2,170m.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong toward the Annapurna Sanctuary — descend to Sinuwa and continue through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest to Dovan (approx. 4-5 hours). The forest is magical — moss-covered trees and the roar of the Modi Khola river below. Wildlife spotting opportunity — Himalayan Thar, langur monkeys, and rare birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (approx. 2 hours) — the landscape becomes increasingly dramatic as the valley narrows. Towering walls of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre close in on either side. Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — a remote and atmospheric stop deep in the Annapurna Sanctuary approach.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in the deep forest — no phone signal, complete immersion in nature. Bonfire (if permitted) or warm fireside at the teahouse. Early rest for tomorrow's push to Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Chomrong teahouse — pancakes, peanut butter, banana, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Sinuwa or Dovan teahouse — hot noodle soup, vegetable fried rice, and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Himalaya Hotel teahouse — hearty dal bhat, vegetable curry, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Today enters the Annapurna Conservation Area more deeply. Permits must be in order (ACAP and TIMS). The bamboo forest section can be slippery — trekking poles essential. Altitude at Himalaya Hotel approximately 2,920m. Temperature drops noticeably.

day_by_day.morning: Summit day to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) — trek from Himalaya Hotel to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m (approx. 3 hours) through increasingly barren high-altitude terrain. The sanctuary opens up dramatically — a glacial amphitheater surrounded by 7,000m and 8,000m peaks on all sides. Continue from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m (approx. 1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — stand at the foot of Annapurna I (8,091m), the world's 10th highest peak. 360-degree views of Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. Private champagne toast at base camp arranged by your guide (carried up in thermos). Photography session — golden afternoon light on the glaciers.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — the peaks turn amber and rose gold. Overnight at ABC teahouse — the highest point of the entire trek. Warm up with hot soup and layers. Early rest — cold temperatures expected (-5°C to -10°C overnight).

meals.breakfast: Himalaya Hotel — high-energy breakfast: oatmeal with nuts and honey, boiled eggs, and hot ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: MBC teahouse — hot soup, energy bars, and thermos tea
meals.dinner: ABC teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable curry, hot chocolate, and energy-rich dessert

day_by_day.notes: THIS IS THE PINNACLE DAY OF THE ENTIRE TRIP. Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m is a profound achievement. Altitude sickness is possible — monitor for headaches, nausea, and dizziness. Descent is the cure if symptoms worsen. Carry altitude sickness medication (Diamox) as prescribed. Dress in maximum layers. The views are utterly transcendent.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at ABC for sunrise over the Annapurna massif — one of the most extraordinary mountain sunrises on the planet. Golden light illuminates the glaciers and 8,000m peaks in an otherworldly display. Photography session with your guide. Hearty breakfast before beginning descent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from ABC through MBC, past Himalaya Hotel, Dovan, and Sinuwa back to Chomrong (approx. 6-7 hours total descent). The descent is significantly faster but requires careful footwork. Arrive in Chomrong — hot shower (if available) and change of clothes. Celebrate the ABC achievement with your guide team.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in Chomrong — celebrate with a special dinner. Hot spring foot soak if available at the teahouse. Reflect on the incredible journey to ABC.

meals.breakfast: ABC teahouse — hot porridge, boiled eggs, toast, and multiple cups of hot tea before descent
meals.lunch: Dovan or Sinuwa teahouse en route — hot noodle soup and vegetable momos
meals.dinner: Chomrong teahouse — celebration dinner: pizza, garlic soup, mixed grill plate, and apple pie with cream

day_by_day.notes: Descent from 4,130m to 2,170m in one day is significant — knees will feel the strain. Trekking poles are essential on the descent. Take your time and rest when needed. Arriving back in Chomrong feels like returning to civilization after the high-altitude sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking morning — leisurely breakfast in Chomrong. Trek down to Jhinu Danda (approx. 1.5 hours) — a small village famous for its natural hot springs directly on the Modi Khola riverbank. Soak in the riverside hot springs — a perfect reward after the ABC achievement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private vehicle transfer arranged from Jhinu Danda / Nayapul to Pokhara (approx. 2-3 hours by jeep). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort — check back in to your Beachfront suite. Luxury spa treatment booked for the afternoon — full body massage, scrub, and facial to rejuvenate after the trek.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Phewa Lake on a private chartered boat. Celebratory gala dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — five-course premium Nepali and continental fusion menu with wine pairing. Toast to an extraordinary Annapurna adventure.

meals.breakfast: Chomrong teahouse — pancakes, fresh fruit, eggs, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant en route to Pokhara or resort room service upon arrival — fresh salads, grilled chicken, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — premium five-course celebration dinner: amuse-bouche, Himalayan trout carpaccio, yak tenderloin, artisan cheese board, and chocolate fondant with Himalayan salt caramel

day_by_day.notes: The return to resort luxury after 10+ days of teahouse trekking will feel extraordinary. Book the spa treatment in advance. The private boat at sunset on Phewa Lake with Machhapuchhre reflected in the water is a magical way to conclude the adventure. Arrange farewell gifts for your guide and porter team — tipping is customary and deeply appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — sleep in and enjoy a luxurious breakfast in bed or on your private terrace. Morning yoga or meditation session by the lake arranged by the resort. Last views of the Annapurna range from the comfort of the resort. Optional final leisure activity: paragliding over Pokhara with Phewa Lake and Himalayan backdrop (world-class paragliding site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at the resort. Leisurely packing and checkout. Private luxury transfer to Pokhara Airport for onward flight to Kathmandu, or direct private vehicle transfer if preferred. Time permitting — final souvenir shopping in Pokhara's lakeside market for Nepali handicrafts, pashmina, and local spices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Pokhara / Kathmandu. Private airport transfer with personal concierge assistance. Farewell from Aegean Bliss Resort team with a parting gift — curated Nepali tea collection and handcrafted memento of your Annapurna journey.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full buffet with live cooking station, fresh Himalayan juices, pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the resort — Nepali thali set with all traditional accompaniments and fresh lassi
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight — departure meal

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits, gear, and souvenirs are packed. Settle guide and porter tips before departure — recommended 10-15% of total trek cost per guide, and USD $8-12 per day per porter. Request a detailed photo album or video compilation of the trip from your guide if arranged.
